newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Cargolux "reasonably optimistic" on 97 rates outlook.
newsitem.headline: Cargolux "reasonably optimistic" on 97 rates outlook.

text.p: Cargolux is "reasonably optimistic" on the outlook for the market rates increases in 1997, the airline's vice-president, Europe, Middle East and Africa, Pierre Wesner told Reuters.
"Traditionally, at this time of the year, load factors and demand are "volatile" following the pre-Christmas and New Year peaks," he said.

"One tell-tale sign of how the market will turn out in the months to come is how quicky these key indicators stabilise and begin to return to "normal' levels and usually by the third to fourth week in January, the picture becomes clearer," Wesner added.

He said: "The gut feeling is that in contrast to the equivalent period in 1996, which saw a deep slump continue well into February, the market will steadily pick-up pace during the fIrst quarter paving the way for rates increases in March and also in the autumn".
"We are simply waiting for some confirmation on this market forecast in the days ahead and will make a definitive decision on rates at the end of January," he added.
Wesner said Cargolux was banking on 1997 growth in freight tonne kilometres (FTK) to be "well in excess of ten percent" on last year's levels.
"1996 will probably show our FTK was up around 10 percent on 1995. However, in terms of financial results it will go down as modest year but not to the point of being negative."
After-tax profits of $11.33 million in 1995 were the second best-ever in the airline's history.

Commenting on Cargolux's freighter network in 1997, Wesner said there was probably some restructuring to be done in the Far East to take into account the weakening of traditional markets and the emergence of new ones and also in the Middle East, where it was seen as a long-term investment.
He also singled out the growth potential in the South American sector.
Cargolux recently decided to invest in two, additional Boeing 747-400Fs during the second half of 1997, as opposed to one, as was initially planned.
The airline currently operates three 747-400Fs and four 747-200Fs. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
